lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: We cannot live next door to Menippus, Pluto. The dog has to move. Put him somewhere else, or we will relocate.
lines.description: outraged tenant complaint, trying to sound dignified

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What exactly is he doing to you? He is just as dead as you are.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we wail and groan about the old days—Midas here about his gold, Sardanapalus about his luxury, me about my treasuries—he laughs at us. He calls us slaves and scum. Sometimes he starts singing and ruins our wailing. The man is a nuisance.
lines.description: sincere grievance, escalating list of injuries

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All true, Pluto. I despise them. They are pathetic, worthless creatures. It wasn't enough for them to live badly; now they have died badly too, and they still cling to the world above. So yes, I enjoy annoying them.
lines.description: cheerfully candid, delighted rather than angry

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: You shouldn't. They are grieving real losses.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Are you losing your mind, Pluto? Siding with their whining?
lines.description: bright disbelief, teasing the authority figure

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Not at all. I just don't want a civil war in the building.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well then, you absolute dregs of Lydia, Phrygia, and Assyria—let me be very clear: I am not stopping. Wherever you go, I will follow. I will annoy you. I will sing over you. I will laugh at you.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. The outrage was what you did. Demanding to be worshipped. Lording it over free men. Never once giving death a single thought. So go ahead and wail. You have been stripped of everything.
lines.description: plain verdict, amused but suddenly sharp

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: So many possessions. [sighs] And all of them great.
lines.description: hollow lament, self-pity returning on cue

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent. Keep going. You mourn, and I will sing 'Know Thyself' as the refrain. It suits this kind of wailing perfectly.
lines.description: pleased conductor of misery, dry punchline
